relationships.subject: migraine
relationships.evidence_quote: GABA+ levels were significantly higher in people with migraine (mean ± SD 4.89 ± 0.62 IU) compared with controls (4.62 ± 0.38 IU) in the PCG

relationships.subject: low back pain
relationships.evidence_quote: GABA+ levels were significantly higher in people with low back pain (mean ± SD 4.88 ± 0.46 IU) compared with controls (4.58 ± 0.34 IU) in the PCG

key_findings: PCG GABA+ (MEGA-PRESS MRS) was significantly higher in migraine and low back pain than controls, with a trend in whiplash-headache.
GABA+ in the ACC did not differ between pain groups and controls; the increase appears general to chronic pain rather than migraine-specific.
